title: Reinstall a dishwasher's two-part filter: lower filter under its tabs, upper filter in and turned to lock
instruction: The bottom of a dishwasher's tub is in front of the robot with its two filters out: the flat lower filter lies on the table beside it and the cylindrical upper filter assembly stands there. Put them back by reversing the maker's removal steps (the upper filter assembly comes out with a quarter turn counterclockwise and a lift, then the lower filter lifts slightly and pulls forward). In this tub two locating tabs at the back of the floor hold the lower filter: push it back under them, so its round opening lines up with the round opening in the bottom of the tub. Insert the upper filter assembly into that opening, turning it until it drops in, then turn it clockwise (seen from above) until it stops, about a quarter turn, so it is locked and no longer turns freely. Then move both grippers at least 10 mm from both filters.
context: Whirlpool's filter help page (producthelp.whirlpool.com, "Cleaning the Filter"): "Remove the filter by turning the Upper Filter Assembly ¼ turn counterclockwise and lifting it out. Grasp the Lower Filter in the circular opening, lift slightly, and pull forward to remove." ... "Reinstall the filter, ensuring it is locked into place." ... "Be sure the Lower Filter is securely in place, and the Upper Filter Assembly is locked into place. If the Upper Filter Assembly turns freely, it is not locked into place." It also says "As a general rule, clean your filter once a month". The task is that reinstall, done as the removal reversed: lower filter back, then the upper filter in and turned clockwise to its stop, a quarter turn. It starts with both filters out and cleaned, beside the tub.
setup: Coordinates: x forward from the arm bases (at y +-0.305), y left, z up from the table; angles about the sump's axis, counterclockwise from +x seen from above, so clockwise is decreasing angle. Fixed: the tub floor, a block 190 x 180 mm with its top 67 mm over the table, its round opening (76 mm across, narrowing to a 69 mm bore 15 mm over the well's floor) at x 0.24, y -0.16 over a sump well 55 mm deep; round the well's floor a bayonet collar with three gaps 30 deg wide at 75, 195, 315 deg, a lip 6 to 9 mm over the floor from each gap's clockwise edge to 100 deg clockwise of its centre, then a stop block to 105 deg; in the well's floor at 0 deg a spring detent pin (150 N/m preloaded 2 mm, its ridge 1.5 mm into the lugs' path, sloped both ways, under the lugs' path between the drop and the lock); on the floor two side rails 1.5 mm outside the lower filter's edges (their inner top edges bevelled 2.5 mm at 45 deg), two runners 1 mm tall under its side edges that it slides on, a rear wall, and two locating tabs at y +-40 mm off the sump's axis that overhang 14 mm forward, 5.5 to 8.5 mm over the floor. Loose: the lower filter (0.06 kg, 150 x 130 x 3 mm, a round opening 76 mm across with a raised ring 8 mm tall round it) flat on the table at x 0.24, y 0.0; the upper filter assembly (0.1 kg, a cylinder 82.5 mm across and 127 mm high with a grip bar across its top, three foot lugs 20 deg wide reaching 33.5 mm from its axis on a neck 57 mm across, under a shoulder where the body widens; seated, the shoulder sits 1 mm over the lower filter's ring) standing at x 0.17, y -0.36. The cup's lugs go down only through the gaps, then a clockwise turn of 90 deg from a gap's centre carries them under the lips, past the pin, to the stop blocks (a cup that dropped off-centre in its gap turns a little more or less to the same stop). The cup's size is the parts listing's 3-1/4 x 5 in; every other size is an estimate.
scoring: The lower filter is home when its centre is within 2 mm of the sump's axis in x and y, its underside within 1.5 mm of its runners' tops, square within 3 deg and tilted under 3 deg (its back is then under both tabs). The upper filter has dropped when its axis is within 3 mm of the sump's, its foot within 1.5 mm of the well's floor and it is tilted under 3 deg; it is locked when dropped, turned to between -2.5 and +2 deg of -15 deg (mod 120: every lug under its lip, past the detent pin). Clear: both grippers' collision hulls 10 mm or more from both filters. Still: both filters under 5 mm/s and 0.05 rad/s. Success (1.0, held 1 s): lower filter home, upper filter locked, clear, still. Partial credit at the last step, each stage needing the one before it: locked, clear and still 0.8; locked and clear 0.7; locked with a hand within 10 mm of a filter (or the hands unread) 0.6; upper filter dropped but not locked 0.5; lower filter home 0.25; else 0. A filter 30 mm below the table top scores 0 from then on.
reset_notes: Lay both filters at their start poses beside the tub; the detent pin starts up. Nothing else moves.
fidelity: Approximate. Whirlpool gives the steps and the quarter turn but no drawings; the cup's size is from a parts listing, and the plate, tabs, collar, lugs, neck and pin are ours. The real lock is a plastic snap; here a sloped spring pin (0.5 N as a lug rides over it) stands in the lugs' path, so a locked cup does not turn freely back. The mesh is solid. The scorer reads poses and hand hulls, not forces.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (2,400 steps); demo: 1.0 (success at 38.95 s, step 779)
